protections: Inline git configuration that sets protocol.*.allow is refused when it arrives as a '-c' switch followed by the config string, unless the caller opts in with unsafe.allowUnsafeProtocolOverride (simple-git/src/lib/plugins/block-unsafe-operations-plugin.ts:6-24, :26-41; docs/PLUGIN-UNSAFE-ACTIONS.md:20-23).

'--upload-pack' is refused in the argv assembled by the clone and fetch tasks, including when it arrives as the positional repo/branch or through an options object (simple-git/src/lib/tasks/clone.ts:32-49; simple-git/src/lib/tasks/fetch.ts:7-24).

traps.reason_to_dismiss: '--config' is a documented, supported clone option that merely writes the new repository's configuration (already exercised with http.extraheader at clone.spec.ts:30-37), so it reads as developer-supplied rather than as inline protocol configuration.

'--config-env' is not an inline '-c' argument; it is an environment indirection the application itself sets up through builder APIs such as .env(), so it looks like application configuration rather than untrusted input.

addConfig (and raw with the config subcommand) is an explicit developer API whose key the caller chooses, so the value being written is treated as intentional configuration rather than argument injection.
Configuration delivered through the child process environment is not an argument at all; the environment is owned by the calling application and .env() is just a builder API.

The shipped guard is attached to clone/fetch; pull, ls-remote and push only talk to an already-configured remote, --upload-pack is a legitimate option for hosts with a non-standard git installation, and raw is documented as unsanitised.
The advisory is about protocol.*.allow; other config keys are the caller's own git configuration, and refusing them would break legitimate setups.

masking: T2 (--config-env) is only visible as a separate hole once T1 (--config) is closed; while '--config' works it is the shorter route to the same sink, so the environment indirection stays unnoticed.

The plugin's own tests only exercise '-c' (simple-git/test/integration/plugin.unsafe.spec.ts:28-55), which hides every non-'-c' configuration route (T1, T2, T4, T6) until the '-c' predicate is recognised as one of several forms.

conflicts.what: A blanket rule that refuses any config-setting argument for T1, or any git config write for T3, would also refuse the legitimate '--config http.extraheader=AUTHORIZATION ...' clone usage (simple-git/test/unit/clone.spec.ts:30-37) and ordinary addConfig usage (simple-git/test/unit/config.spec.ts:63-91); both fixes must match the key/protocol prefix rather than ban the mechanism.

The natural fix for T5 and T6 is to deny more option/config-key names; done broadly it refuses inputs legitimate users need (custom --upload-pack paths, '-c core.sshCommand=<custom ssh>'), which is exactly the over-hardening failure mode, so both need the same opt-in flag as the protocol guard.

fairness_risks: clone's '--config <key>=<value>' is a supported and tested shape for secrets such as http.extraheader (simple-git/test/unit/clone.spec.ts:30-37); a security rule that refuses '--config' as an option contradicts that legitimate use, so the rule has to be key-scoped.

addConfig is a general-purpose API with global/system/local scopes (simple-git/src/lib/tasks/config.ts:7-12, :24-45, :81-91) and its own tests (simple-git/test/unit/config.spec.ts:91); refusing all config writes is not viable and refusing protocol.* keys outright contradicts users who intentionally enable protocol.file.allow for submodules.

--upload-pack is legitimate when git-upload-pack is not on PATH; clone/fetch block it only when the caller supplies it and offer no opt-in for that guard (simple-git/src/lib/tasks/clone.ts:46-49), so extending it to pull/ls-remote/push removes a working capability unless the same opt-in pattern is added.
.env() with git's environment-configuration variables is a normal CI setup path (simple-git/src/git.js:85-93); a rule that refuses environment-supplied configuration contradicts that use.

Refused input shapes that legitimate uses also need: '--config http.extraheader=...', 'addConfig("user.name", ...)', '--upload-pack=/opt/git/bin/git-upload-pack', and '-c core.sshCommand=<path to ssh>' for a custom ssh binary.

The short form '-u' and case/whitespace variants of '-c protocol...' are spelling/encoding variants and are deliberately not recorded as traps; a fix that normalises them must still allow the long-form legitimate uses.

design.why: These four sit in four different layers and each has its own reason to dismiss, so a solver cannot close them with one insight: (T1) the argv predicate in the unsafe plugin keys on '-c' and misses clone's own '--config'/'-c'-free config shape, with the added trap that the tested legitimate '--config http.extraheader' must keep working (a coupled value, the MiMo failure mode); (T3) the same capability through the config-writing API, dismissed as 'explicit developer intent' (DeepSeek's absent-protection-with-a-reason pattern); (T4) the out-of-band environment route, which the spawn.args plugin structurally cannot see (simple-git/src/lib/plugins/simple-git-plugin.ts:14); and (T5) the --upload-pack guard that exists in clone and fetch but not in the sibling tasks, the classic parallel-entry decision. It beats a T1+T2-only design, which is one predicate and two spellings of the same option; it beats adding T6, whose 'refuse other exec-capable config keys' rule is both outside the protocol advisory's scope and directly contradicts legitimate '-c core.sshCommand' use; and it beats a T3+T4-only design, which would have no argv-layer trap at all. Every chosen trap is testable through the existing plugin-error and configuration-error machinery (simple-git/test/integration/plugin.unsafe.spec.ts:28-55; simple-git/test/unit/clone.spec.ts:62-86), and the instance-level 'config' option is deliberately not a trap because the prefix plugin runs before the unsafe plugin (simple-git/src/lib/git-factory.ts:55-59; simple-git/src/lib/plugins/plugin-store.ts:27-31; simple-git/src/lib/utils/util.ts:135-140).

git-side semantics that make the non-'-c' routes dangerous are external to the repository: that 'git clone --config <key>=<value>' takes effect before the initial fetch; that '--config-env' and the GIT_CONFIG_COUNT/GIT_CONFIG_KEY_n/GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_n environment protocol exist; that pull and ls-remote accept --upload-pack and push accepts --receive-pack; and that keys such as core.sshCommand, core.fsmonitor and uploadpack.packObjectsHook execute programs.

Whether GHSA-hffm-xvc3-vprc's published fix covers only the clone '--config' shape or also the --config-env, config-write, environment and sibling-task routes is unknown; T2-T6 are candidate traps from the same protection family, not confirmed from the advisory text.

The plugin also throws for '-c protocol...' after the subcommand (simple-git/test/integration/plugin.unsafe.spec.ts:36-42), a position git itself ignores for that option; that case is over-blocking rather than a missing protection and is not counted as a trap.
